statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-44973: github.com/go-git/go-billy/v5 before 5.9.0 does not consistently stop crafted paths (for example ones using ..) from escaping the base directory of its osfs and helper/chroot filesystems; it is fixed in 5.9.0 (https://github.com/go-git/go-billy/security/advisories/GHSA-qw64-3x98-g7q2, https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5597, https://github.com/go-git/go-billy/releases/tag/v5.9.0). Each of the 38 published trivy-dev builds for Alpine 3.23 (0.69.1-r0 to 0.74.0-r12), on both x86_64 and aarch64, was downloaded, checked against the repository index checksum and read for this decision; each holds one file, /usr/bin/trivy, a statically linked Go binary. Its Go build information shows github.com/go-git/go-billy/v5 5.7.0 to 5.8.0 in builds before 0.70.0-r1 and 5.9.0 to 5.9.2 from 0.70.0-r1 on, and no github.com/go-git/go-billy/v6 in any build. The Go symbol table (go tool nm function entries) of every build contains functions the advisory lists as vulnerable: osfs.New, osfs.BoundOS.Chroot and helper/chroot.ChrootHelper.Chroot, with runtime.main found in each binary as a control, so the vulnerable package is linked and the fixed version is the first build carrying go-billy 5.9.0.
